candidates.computation_change_reason: Column headers define how instream waste concentrations and multiple domestic/aquatic/human-health criteria are derived from ambient (Ca), effluent (Ce), and formula terms (e.g., 2.13*Ce, Cd,dom). A different reading of which column is operative, or how formulas map to enforceable limits, would change which numeric limit is selected for compliance comparison.

The MQL column appears alongside each pollutant with numeric values (e.g., 0.005, 0.5, 5). Interpretation of MQL as a method quantitation/detection threshold could change whether reported measurements are comparable to limits, whether monitoring at that sensitivity was required, and how sub-MQL or missing results are classified.

The parenthetical (P) on this pollutant row may denote a provisional, potential, or specially conditioned parameter. If (P) changes which criteria values are enforceable or whether monitoring for this form is required, the applicable limit and monitoring obligation for nickel would change.

Same as other (P)-marked rows: the (P) qualifier may signal a distinct regulatory status or applicability condition for this pollutant form, affecting which numeric criteria apply and whether monitoring for thallium dissolved is obligatory.

This row names a sulfate-conditioned selenium variant with its own criteria values (e.g., Irrigation 250 vs 130 for ordinary dissolved selenium). Whether SO4 exceeds 500 mg/l determines which limit row applies and whether monitoring under this conditional parameter is required.

This row mixes finite criteria (1.4 chronic aquatic, 0.77 human health) with 1E+100 placeholders in other columns. Interpreting 1E+100 as non-applicable versus a literal numeric limit would change which enforceable limit is selected and whether a measurement exceeds it.

Dissolved versus total mercury rows carry different operative criteria (e.g., domestic 2 vs 1E+100; chronic aquatic 1E+100 vs 1.4). Which mercury speciation is the monitored/enforceable parameter determines the applicable limit and monitoring requirement.

The Need TMDL column appears for every pollutant with value N/A. If N/A means no TMDL-driven limit is needed versus unknown or deferred TMDL applicability, the set of enforceable limits and unresolved cases would differ.

Ce (effluent concentration) and Ca (ambient concentration) cells are blank while other columns contain 0 or 1E+100. Whether blanks mean no data, zero, or not applicable affects baseline effluent used in limit derivation and how missing-evidence cases are classified.

Multiple finite criteria appear simultaneously (domestic 700, acute aquatic 923.8432611, chronic aquatic 102.610464, human health 4600). Which criterion endpoint governs compliance for a given discharge/receiving-water use would change the applicable enforceable limit.

Both formula-derived instream concentrations (e.g., 2.13*Ce ≈ 1.362944268) and separate use-specific criteria columns (e.g., irrigation 25000, acute aquatic 332.1857266) are populated. Interpreting which value is the binding enforceable limit would change exceedance determinations.

1E+100 appears throughout criteria columns as a recurring placeholder. Treating it as no numeric limit, a de minimis sentinel, or missing data would change whether compliance comparisons are applicable and how no-result or below-threshold cases are categorized.
